Definition: Bashan (often with the article), a region East of the Jordan
BiblicalUsage: Bashan is the rich land east of the Jordan, the kingdom of Og, whose cities and oaks and strong bulls are named again and again. Israel turns to fight Og at Edrei, takes all his cities and his land, and divides Bashan among the half-tribe of Manasseh.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Bashan stands in Scripture for strength that cannot save, because Og's bed was made of iron and his kingdom was still given into Israel's hand. The oaks are tall and the bulls are strong, and I hold that none of it matters when God has given the land to His people.
